offer.say: get a job offer · make an offer · accept an offer
offer.note: Most often "offer" is a verb: "Can I offer you some tea?"
ex: I got a job offer today!
Did you accept their offer?
They made me a good offer.
Can I think about your offer?

Mrs..say: Mrs. Brown · Mr. and Mrs. Brown
Mrs..note: Used before a married woman's last name. "Ms." is safe for any woman.

detail.say: in detail · the details of · more details
ex: Send me the details, please.
I need more details about the job.
Can you tell me the details?
Check every detail before you pay.

manager.say: talk to the manager · the store manager

role.say: play a role · the main role · a role in
ex: What is your role in the team?
She plays the main role in this film.
My role at work is very important.
Who plays the role of the doctor?

partner.say: a business partner · work with a partner

ex: I like your style.
What style of music do you like?
Do you have this shoe in another style?
She has great style.

product.say: a new product · buy a product
product.note: Food from a store is "groceries," not "products."

ha.note: "Ha ha" shows laughing; it can also mean you are not amused.
ex: Ha! That's so funny!
Ha ha, very funny.
Ha! I win again!
Ha, are you serious?

surprise.say: What a surprise! · a surprise party · have a surprise for

minister.say: prime minister · the minister of health

client.say: meet a client · a new client

football.note: In the US, "football" means American football. Soccer is "soccer".

model.say: a new model · a fashion model · a car model

ex: He is a real gentleman.
Good evening, ladies and gentlemen!
A gentleman is waiting for you outside.
Can you help this gentleman, please?

weekend.say: on the weekend · this weekend · at the weekend (UK)

training.say: a training course · job training · get training
training.note: Uncountable: say "a training course," not "a training." It also means sports practice.
ex: The training starts at ten.
Is the training free for new workers?
We have safety training at work today.
Can I join the training next week?

lunch.say: have lunch · for lunch · at lunch
lunch.note: Usually no "a": "have lunch," not "have a lunch."

contract.say: sign a contract · a work contract

site.say: on the site · visit a site
site.note: It can also mean a place: "a construction site," "a camping site."
ex: I buy shoes on this site.
Can you send me a link to the site?
The site does not open on my phone.
Is this site safe for payments?

trip.say: go on a trip · take a trip · a business trip

activity.note: Often means action in general: "physical activity," "brain activity."

course.say: take a course · an English course · of course
course.note: Most often in "of course" (= yes, sure): "Can I sit here?" "Of course!"

band.say: play in a band · a rock band

idiot.note: Rude word; be careful using it about other people.

period.say: a period of time · for a short period
period.note: In American English, "period" is also the dot at the end of a sentence (.).
ex: It is a busy period at work.
Summer is a busy period for hotels.
Can I pay over a period of six months?
I lived there for a short period.
The prince lives in a big castle.
Kids love stories about a prince and a princess.
The prince visited our city today.
Who plays the prince in this film?

interview.say: give an interview · do an interview · an interview with
interview.note: Often a job interview: "I have a job interview tomorrow."
ex: I read an interview with the singer.
The interview is on TV tonight.
Can we do a short interview?
She gave an interview to a newspaper.

center.say: in the center · the city center · a shopping center
ex: The hotel is in the city center.
How do I get to the center?
Is the shopping center open today?
I live near the center.

goodbye.note: "Bye" is more common in casual speech.
ex: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
She said goodbye and left.
We waved goodbye to our friends.
Did you say goodbye to Grandma?

type.say: a type of · this type of
type.note: Also a verb: "type" a message on a keyboard. In speech, "kind" is more common.
ex: What type of music do you like?
This type of phone is very cheap.
What type of room do you need?
We sell all types of bread.

text.say: read the text · in the text
text.note: In everyday talk, "a text" often means a phone message (SMS).

internet.say: on the internet · use the internet

speech.say: give a speech · make a speech
ex: He gave a short speech at the wedding.
I have to make a speech tomorrow.
Her speech was very funny.
Can you help me write my speech?

skill.say: learn a skill · computer skills · skills for
ex: What skills do you need for this job?
Cooking is a useful skill.
I want to learn new skills.
Put your computer skills on your resume.

crazy.note: Informal. Don't use it about people with mental illness.
ex: This is a crazy idea!
Are you crazy? It is very cold!
The traffic is crazy today.
Don't do anything crazy, OK?

contact.note: Also a verb: "Please contact us by email."

tour.say: go on a tour · take a tour · on tour

comment.say: leave a comment · a comment on

actor.say: a famous actor · my favorite actor
ex: She wants to be an actor.
The actor was very good in that film.
Who is your favorite actor?
Many famous actors live in this city.

episode.say: the first episode · the next episode

document.say: sign a document · print a document

expert.say: an expert in · ask an expert

method.say: a method of · a new method

lord.note: Most often "Lord" means God: "Thank the Lord!" A lord is also a British noble.
ex: The lord lives in a big castle.
Is he a real lord?
The old lord has a lot of land.
My grandfather worked for a rich lord.

lieutenant.say: a police lieutenant · an army lieutenant
ex: My brother is a lieutenant in the army.
The lieutenant gives orders to the soldiers.
Where is the lieutenant?
Lieutenant, can I ask a question?

round.say: the first round · the next round
round.note: Often an adjective: "a round table" (in the shape of a circle).
ex: He won the fight in the third round.
Our team is in the next round.
Who won the first round?
The second round starts in five minutes.

brand.say: a brand of · a good brand

ex: My little girl is an angel.
There is an angel on top of our tree.
You're an angel, thank you!
Can you draw an angel for me?

assistant.say: a personal assistant · a teaching assistant
assistant.note: In British English, a "shop assistant" is a person who sells things in a store.
ex: Ask my assistant to call you back.
She works as a teaching assistant.
My assistant will send you the documents.
Is your assistant in the office today?

ocean.say: in the ocean · the Atlantic Ocean
ex: We swam in the ocean every day.
The hotel has a view of the ocean.
Is the ocean warm in June?
I love the sound of the ocean.
Suicide is a serious problem.
If you think about suicide, please talk to someone.
The film is about suicide.
Doctors can help people who think about suicide.

detective.say: a private detective · a police detective
detective.note: For a book or film, say "a detective story," not "a detective."
ex: The detective asked many questions.
She hired a private detective.
Do you like detective films?
I love reading detective stories.

foot.say: six feet tall · ten feet long
foot.note: Most often "foot" is the body part: "My foot hurts." As a unit, 1 foot = 30 cm.
ex: He is six feet tall.
The room is twelve feet long.
How tall are you in feet?
This box is one foot wide.

hmm.note: Informal; used in speech or texts.
ex: Hmm, which one should I buy?
Hmm, let me think for a minute.
Hmm, that sounds strange.
Hmm, are you sure about this?

yo.note: Very informal slang greeting; avoid in formal situations.
